findings.title: Opening door leaves hide Pip at every side-wall door and half-hide Pip at back-wall doors
findings.problem: When Pip walks up to a door, its leaf springs open (src/hub/lobby.ts:128-130, rotation.y = -open*1.25 about a hinge at local x -0.84, line 90). The leaf swings out into the lobby, toward the camera. On the three left-wall doors (Fabrication Bay, Signal Observatory, Spectrum Delivery) the hinge is on the camera side, so the open leaf sits between the camera and the spot where Pip has to stand (door.at = x+1.1). At the default camera only Pip's yellow ring shows: lobby-play-14 at QFN, lobby-play-15 at Spectrum, lobby-play-16 at zoom 9 (Pip is gone completely), and lobby-play-36 on a phone (a sliver of blue). On back-wall doors the leaf covers Pip's left half at the default yaw (lobby-play-31, Arcade Rush) and all of Pip after a small orbit (lobby-play-12, Playground door: only the leaf and the marker tip show). Leaves are not in game.occluders (src/game.ts:387-388 fades occluders only; lobby.ts never registers any), so nothing fades. This happens at the hub's one core moment, choosing a door: the player loses their avatar right when the prompt appears and can't see the portal glimpse that is meant to sell the destination. It breaks AGENTS 8 and DR-12. It also wastes the portal effect (DR-13: the target, the doorway, is hidden by its own door).
findings.fix: In src/hub/lobby.ts door() (line 90), stop the leaf from swinging into the camera's view. (a) Preferred: open every door inward, into the corridor. Use leaf.rotation.y=+open*1.25 in update() (line 130) and set leaf material depthTest so the wall hides it. The portal plane at z .05 already shows the corridor, so the leaf can simply hide once open>0.5 (leaf.visible=open<0.5) after a quick inward swing. (b) If the outward swing stays, mirror the hinge on side doors: leaf group at lx +0.84, leaf geometry offset -0.83, and rotation.y=+open*1.25, so the leaf opens toward world -z, behind Pip from a +z camera. Also push the leaf's meshes into game.occluders with a transparent clone of the glossyToon material, so the existing fade catches them. Also change the occlusion ray to sample feet, chest and head (DR-12), not only p.y+.4.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lobby-play/b-doors.mjs and retake lobby-play-14/15/16 and the phone shot 36. At least 70% of Pip's pixels should be visible at every door, and the portal's destination glimpse should be visible past Pip. Add a check to tests/lobby.spec.ts: at each door.at, raycast from the camera to Pip's head, chest and feet, with no unfaded hit.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. In verify-lobby-play-02 (Pip parked at the Fabrication Bay door, door settled at open=1, default camera), only the yellow ring and a sliver of Pip show past the open leaf. I cast rays from the camera to Pip's feet, chest and head against hub.doors[].leaf, and all three hit the leaf. lobby-play-14 and lobby-play-16 (zoom 9: the leaf fills the view and Pip is gone) are as described. G.occluders.length is 0 in the lobby, so nothing fades. At the Playground back door with default yaw, none of the three rays hit the leaf, so the back-wall problem is partial and depends on yaw, which matches lobby-play-31 and lobby-play-12. Code: the hinge group is at lx -0.84 (src/hub/lobby.ts:90) and update() sets rotation.y=-open*1.25 (:130). The fix is sound.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lobby-play/v1.mjs log: qfn blockedFeetChestHead [true,true,true], occluders 0; Playground door [false,false,false]

findings.title: The objective marker over the next door is a pale 20 px cone that blends into the door panel
findings.problem: The hub only has to answer one question: which door next? The answer is the marker cone (src/ui/objectives.ts:98: ConeGeometry r .22 h .42, MeshBasicMaterial #ffd84a with its outline turned off), placed at the step's at() point, y 2.1±0.18 (objectives.ts:118). At the default lobby camera (zoom 23) it is about 20×18 px, pale yellow with no ink outline. It sits inside the door frame over the teal window panel, below the name plate, so it reads as a sticker on the door (crops lobby-play-09 and lobby-play-21). On the start frame the target door, 00 Cable Playground, is in the far top-left corner next to the objective card, and nothing else in the frame points there. At zoom 9 and in the high orbit (lobby-play-05, lobby-play-07) no door is on screen at all and there is no edge arrow. On a phone (lobby-play-34, -35) the target door is off-screen. This breaks DR-44 (at least 24 px, outlined, 2-tone, above clutter) and DR-13 (the target is never hidden or lost).
findings.fix: In src/ui/objectives.ts: scale the hub marker (or all markers) to r .4 and h .75 and float it above the door header, at y = 3.0 + bounce for hub steps (the lamp is at 3.35, so 3.7 for hub doors; add an optional `markerY` to the step interface, from Lobby.job.steps at()). Make it 2-tone: a ToonMaterial body plus an inverted-hull ink outline (set outlineParameters visible:true with the INK colour). Add a soft ground ring (the reticle style, #ffd84a, about 1.4 m) at door.at so the floor spot reads too. Add a screen-edge chevron in the HUD layer when the marker's projected position is outside the viewport: project it each frame, clamp it to a 24 px inset, and rotate it toward the target. That covers zoom 9, orbits and phones.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-01 and the crop at the target door: the marker is at least 24 px tall with a dark outline, above the name plate. Retake lobby-play-07 (zoom 9) and lobby-play-34 (phone): an edge arrow points toward door 00.
findings.verify_reason: I projected the marker cone at the start view. It is 21 px tall, its top at screen y 16 and x 271, inside the Playground door frame, with outlineParameters {visible:false}. That is under DR-44's 24 px and has no outline. In the survey it shrinks to about 15 px. The code matches src/ui/objectives.ts:97-98 (MeshBasicMaterial, outline off, r .22 h .42) and :118 (y 2.1±0.18). Crop lobby-play-21 shows a pale cone over the teal panel. In lobby-play-07 (zoom 9) and on the phone (lobby-play-34) no door or arrow is on screen.

findings.title: The start frame hides the left-wall doors under the job card, leaves the bottom third empty, and can't show all 9 doors
findings.problem: L1 (R3A M8) asked that the first frame show every door. It is still not met. At 1440×900 the job card (top-left) covers the three left-wall doors. In the crop lobby-play-50, only the blade signs '05 · Fabrication Bay' and '06 · Signal Observatory' peek out above the card, at about 4 px cap height, and Spectrum Delivery is not visible at all. Meanwhile rows about 600–900 of the frame (about a third) are empty planks, the front lip and void (lobby-play-01). The camera aims at the generic room point (.2,0,1) (src/game.ts:367) at homeZoom 23 (src/game.ts:397), which suits a room whose interest is in the middle, but the lobby's content is all on the back and left walls. Zooming out to 38 makes it worse: the back-wall name plates are cut off by the top of the screen (lobby-play-08). A new player can't see a third of the jobs on arrival.
findings.fix: Pick one, or combine: (1) Give the hub its own camera anchor in src/game.ts updateCamera. When this.hub is set, use room = (-2.5,0,-3.5) instead of (.2,0,1), default yaw about 0.35 (turned toward the left wall) and homeZoom 26, so the back and left walls fill the upper two-thirds and the empty front lip drops off the bottom. (2) Re-slot the doors in src/hub/lobby.ts slots() (l.24-30) so no door sits behind the top-left HUD: put all 9 on the back wall at 3.0 m spacing (30 m wall, 2.12 m frames), or 6 back plus 3 on the right wall (the card is on the left). Then delete the unused 'free' slot code and its stale comment (l.23, 28, 79). (3) Make the job card narrower in the hub, or move it down while the start view is up.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-01: all 9 name plates are visible and none is under any HUD element. Less than 15% of the frame is empty floor or void (measure rows below the floor lip). Retake lobby-play-08 at zoom 38: the signs are not cut off.
findings.verify_reason: lobby-play-01 and crop lobby-play-50 show the job card covering the left-wall doors. Only the Fabrication and Observatory blade signs peek out, and the Spectrum door is cut off. Rows below about 620 px are the floor lip and void. The camera code matches src/game.ts:367 (room .2,0,1) and :397 (hub zoom 23). I lowered the priority to P2. The Tab survey (lobby-play-02) shows all 9 doors clearly. The current target, door 00, plus the marker and the directory board are visible on the start frame. This hurts first-glance clarity but doesn't noticeably block understanding.

findings.title: Phone survey (Tab) and phone start show 3 of 9 doors, and the current target is off-screen
findings.problem: At 390×844 the start frame shows Big Meeting, Lunch Rush and part of Arcade (lobby-play-34). The survey that should show the whole room (DR-21) shows the same three doors and the reception (lobby-play-35). The target door 00, the three side doors and Robot Garage are all off-screen. The survey zoom is a fixed 44 (src/game.ts:366) and doesn't adapt to aspect, and in portrait the follow factor is forced to 1 (follow=cam.aspect<1?1:..., game.ts:366), so the survey keeps centring the room at the 16:10 yaw. A phone player can't find most of the jobs, or the one the card tells them to do, without walking around blind.
findings.fix: In src/game.ts updateCamera, when survey && cam.aspect<1: turn the survey yaw by π/2 so the room's 30 m axis runs up the screen. Compute the distance that fits the room's bounds, distance = max(level.width,level.depth)*0.5/tan(min(vfov,hfov)/2)*1.1, clamped to ≤ 80, or raise the survey FOV to 45° in portrait. Do the same for the hub start pose. Pair this with the edge arrow from the marker finding.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/lobby-play/e-phone.mjs. lobby-play-35 should show all four walls and all 9 doors, and lobby-play-34 should show the target door or an arrow to it.
findings.verify_reason: At 390×844 I projected each door.at at y 1.5. At start only lunch is in frame, and in the survey only lunch and arcade are, with meeting partly cut at the edge in lobby-play-35. Door 00, the target, is off-screen in both. This breaks DR-21 outright. One part of the diagnosis is wrong. In survey, target=room.lerp(pip, survey?0:follow) (src/game.ts:368), so `follow` (forced to 1 in portrait) plays no part in the survey framing. The real causes are the fixed zoom 44 and the yaw .14 (16:10) at a portrait aspect.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lobby-play/v2.mjs log: phone start only lunch:IN; phone survey lunch:IN arcade:IN, others out
src/game.ts:368 (survey lerps 0 toward Pip, so follow is irrelevant there)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the fix, but drop the follow-factor rationale. The survey ignores `follow` (src/game.ts:368). In portrait, the fix should only change the survey and hub-start yaw/distance (and/or FOV).

findings.title: The hub is an empty hall: 15 props in 600 m², no cable, no chaos target, nothing happens without the player
findings.problem: The lobby is the first room every player stands in and the one they come back to most. It has 15 props (src/levels/lobby.ts:4-9: 4 plants, a cooler, a bin, 2 boxes, 2 chairs, a beanbag, a cone, a mug, 2 papers), 3 idle coworkers, and no `clutter` config, across a 30×20 m floor. The survey (lobby-play-02) reads as a bare dance floor. There is no cable at all (the cable is hidden and not simulated in the hub, src/game.ts:92/104), so the game's star mechanic is absent from its front door (AGENTS 4, DR-05). There is no chaos bonus or physical goal (the bonuses are all meta, lobby.ts:44-47, against DR-10). Nothing funny happens in the first 30 s unless the player goes looking (DR-03). The chaos that does exist works well: a thrown chair flies over the desk, the receptionist pops the '!' alarm bubble and damage ticks (lobby-play-23, alarmed 1, fastestProp 8.4). There just isn't enough to throw. AGENTS 3 asks for hundreds of props. The product owner needs to rule on a hub exemption (L7, DR-67), but even an exempt hub should be a toy box, not a corridor.
findings.fix: (1) Add `clutter:{seed:7,max:130,recipes:['waiting','mail','deliveries']}` to src/levels/lobby.ts, plus themed clusters at each wing door from the wing's own room: crates of arcade tokens at 03, a tyre stack at 04, tray carts at 02, server boxes at 01, a cone-and-spool pile at 00. Keep a 2.5 m clear lane from spawn to each door.at (DR-16). (2) Add a hub cable toy: a short 8 m reel beside reception with a socket on the HQ sign. Plugging it in lights 'CIRCUIT CREW HQ' and plays a jingle, so the first thing a new player can do in the game is the cable act (enable simulateCable/drawCable for the hub when level.length>0; src/game.ts:104). (3) Add one physical bonus to the hub job that replaces the duplicate 'Light every wing' (see the separate finding), e.g. 'Knock the visitor-cone pyramid over' using the bowling-pin code from the Playground (game.ts pinsDown).
findings.verify: Retake the survey: at least 120 props, each 4×4 m walkable cell has 3 or more, and the clear lanes to doors still pass a walkTo replay. A new spec, tests/lobby.spec.ts 'hub reel lights the sign', reaches snap().rope.maxLength>0 and the sign lit.
findings.verify_reason: src/levels/lobby.ts:4-9 has exactly 15 props and no `clutter` key. The plug, target and socket are hidden, and the cable isn't simulated or drawn in the hub (src/game.ts:92, :104). All three bonuses are meta (src/hub/lobby.ts:44-47). The survey shot shows a bare floor. Chaos works: the chair throw alarmed an NPC in lobby-play-23. The proposed fix uses clutter recipes that don't exist. 'waiting', 'mail' and 'deliveries' are not in the Recipe union (src/levels/clutter.ts:11), so that config would fail type-check. P1 is defensible because the hub is the first and most-revisited room, but the DR-67/DR-05 applicability still needs the product owner's hub-exemption ruling.
extra_evidence: src/levels/clutter.ts:11 (valid recipes: crates, pod, lounge, bins, cones, cart, shelf, cooler, reading, parts, plants, cabinets, box, litter, cone, bin)
src/game.ts:77 (clutter applies to any level with level.clutter, so the hub would accept it)
findings.fix_correction: Use existing recipes, e.g. `clutter:{seed:7,max:130,step:2.1,recipes:['lounge','plants','crates','cooler','reading','bins','lounge','crates'],fill:['box','litter','cone']}`. Add new 'mail' or 'deliveries' recipes to src/levels/clutter.ts RECIPES only if you want them. Keep 2.5 m lanes to each door.at as stated.

findings.title: Entering a door is an instant page reload, and coming back is a reset to spawn: no transition, no return payoff
findings.problem: Pressing E at a door calls location.href right away (src/hub/lobby.ts:123). It sets hud.dataset.leaving, but no CSS or code reads `data-leaving` (grep shows only this line), so Pip doesn't step into the corridor, the screen doesn't fade, and the job simply replaces the lobby about 1.4 s later (lobby-play-51 shows the Meeting already loaded). Going back through pause → Jobs reloads the lobby with Pip at the centre spawn (0,5.5), not at the door he left (lobby-play-53, player 0/5.5). A freshly earned medal or lit wing lamp is already there on load, with no lamp ignition, cheer or confetti. The hub's main reward moment, 'a wing lights up when repaired' (header comment at lobby.ts:1-3), never actually happens on screen. DR-11 asks for juicy, framed success moments.
findings.fix: In Lobby.enter: lock input and walk Pip 1.2 m into the doorway over 0.5 s (drive the player body toward door.at - wallNormal*1.2). Ramp portal uOpen to 1.5 and add a CSS fade on `body .hud[data-leaving]` (wing colour → black, 400 ms), then navigate. Before navigating, store sessionStorage 'circuit-crew:from'=level.id. In Lobby's constructor and game spawn, if 'from' is set, spawn Pip at that door's at, facing the room. If record() reported first/improved (store a 'circuit-crew:new-medal' flag in game-ui won()), play an ignition beat: the lamp scales 0→1.3→1 with hot() emissive, the glow fades in, a confetti burst comes from the door, nearby coworkers cheer (npc cheer path) and the medal plate flips in.
findings.verify: A script: enter the playground, finish it via the routes.spec path, press Jobs. The lobby starts with Pip at the playground door and the lamp-ignite burst is visible in a screenshot about 0.5 s in. Check a fade frame on the way in.
findings.verify_reason: Grepping src for 'leaving' (TS and CSS) finds only the setter at src/hub/lobby.ts:123. Nothing reads data-leaving, so there is no fade or walk-in. The lobby always spawns at level.spawn (src/game.ts:81), and the store has no 'from' key (src/ui/store.ts:20-21 holds only the autostart flag). Lamps are built already lit at load (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97), so the player never sees an ignition beat.

findings.title: Door names, numbers, medals and LOCKED tags are too small to read at the game camera
findings.problem: Signs are how the player picks a job, but at the default camera the name plates have about 5 px cap height for long names ('Overheating Arcade', fitted to a 1.95 m plate) and about 8 px for short ones ('Arcade Rush'). The leaf number ('03') is about 4 px, the LOCKED tag about 4 px, and the medal letters (0.34 m plates) about 6 px (crop lobby-play-49 at 3×; lobby-play-29). DR-48 asks for at least 14 px cap height on any text the player must read. Right now the player has to walk up to each door and read the prompt pill to know what it is. The directory board above reception repeats every name at about 5 px (lobby-play-01), so it adds noise without helping.
findings.fix: In src/hub/lobby.ts door(): make the name plate frame-wide, 2.3 m × 0.5 m at y 2.95 on top of the header, tilted 12° down toward the camera, with a fixed font height so long names wrap to two lines instead of shrinking. Put the number into a big round badge on the header (0.5 m) in the wing colour. Make the medal plate 0.6 m and place it on the header next to the badge. Replace the LOCKED text tag with a 0.6 m padlock prop plus a chain or tape across the frame. Either drop the directory board or shrink it to numbers plus wing-colour chips (no text).
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-01 and crop every plate: the name cap height is at least 14 px at 1440×900 for all 9 doors, and the medal letter is at least 14 px.
findings.verify_reason: In lobby-play-01 at 1440×900, the back-wall name plates are about 5–8 px cap height ('Overheating Arcade' is the smallest). The leaf numbers and the LOCKED tag are about 4 px, and the medal letters in lobby-play-29 are about 6 px. All fall short of DR-48's 14 px. The plate sizes in code match src/hub/lobby.ts:91-94.

findings.title: Side-door blade signs cut through the edge-on wall plate, so each side door has two signs, one unreadable
findings.problem: Side doors still get the frame title plate on the wall (lobby.ts:92), which reads edge-on from the atrium, plus the newer blade sign (lobby.ts:82, group at s.x+.95, plate 1.7 m wide at y 2.86). The blade plate spans world x -14.9…-13.2 and passes through the wall plate at x about -14.7. The blade's first characters are hidden inside the edge-on plate ('6 · Signal Observatory' in lobby-play-40, and '07 · Spectrum Delivery' clipped by the 'Spectrum Deliv…' plate in lobby-play-16). Each side door shows a readable sign crossed with an unreadable one (lobby-play-10, -14). The bracket arm ends at x -14.7, short of the wall face, and reads as hanging in the air next to the lamp.
findings.fix: In src/hub/lobby.ts:92, skip `signPlate(f,title(level)…)` when s.wall==='side' (the blade replaces it), or raise it to y 2.56 → 2.3 so it clears the blade. Move the blade group so its plate starts at the wall: use group x = s.x + 0.15 + 1.7/2 = s.x+1.0, and extend the bracket arm to x = s.x (the wall face) with a small wall plate (DR-72). Raise the blade to y 3.05 so it doesn't collide with the header.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-40 and -16: each side door shows exactly one fully readable sign, and the blade's bracket touches the wall.
findings.verify_reason: In lobby-play-40, the blade plate shows '6 · Signal Observatory' and '5 · Fabrication Bay', with the leading digit swallowed by the frame title plate. In lobby-play-14 and verify-lobby-play-02, the wall plates read edge-on as slivers next to the readable blades. Geometry: the blade group is at s.x+.95 = x -14.05 with a 1.7 m plate (x -14.9…-13.2) (src/hub/lobby.ts:82). The frame plate sits at about x -14.7 (f at z .14 plus plate z .16, :92), so the two intersect.

findings.title: Locked door feedback is invisible: the E 'jiggle' is overwritten the next frame, and the lock barely reads
findings.problem: Pressing E at the locked Arcade Rush door sets d.leaf.rotation.y=-.08 (src/hub/lobby.ts:121). Lobby.update() then sets leaf.rotation.y=-d.open*1.25 every frame (l.130), and open is 0 for a locked door, so the jiggle never renders. The only feedback is a 140 Hz tone and the prompt (lobby-play-13, taken 0.15 s after E: the door is still). From the atrium the lock state is a 4 px 'LOCKED' tag and a small yellow square over the 03R panel (crop lobby-play-49). The door otherwise looks the same as an open job, apart from a slightly greyer portal that only shows when it would open. DR-47 asks that a device show its state on the device itself. DR-19 asks that the key do something visible.
findings.fix: Add `rattle:number` to Door. In interact set d.rattle=.4. In update, leaf.rotation.y = -d.open*1.25 + Math.sin(time*45)*.05*d.rattle/.4, with d.rattle decaying by dt. Add a puff and a red pulse on the padlock, and play Pip's shrug (game.shrug()). Make the lock read from afar: a 0.6 m padlock prop on the leaf, hazard tape across the frame, and the portal shown dark even when closed.
findings.verify: Script: at the rush door press E, then advance(.1) and shot. The leaf is visibly rotated or rattling and the padlock flashes. The locked door is identifiable in lobby-play-01 without zooming.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced at runtime. Right after E at the locked Arcade Rush door, leaf.rotation.y is -0.08. After one 0.05 s advance it is back to 0, because update() rewrites it every frame (src/hub/lobby.ts:121 vs :130). The only feedback left is the tone and the prompt ('Locked: finish 03 · Overheating Arcade first'). In lobby-play-01 the lock reads only as the tiny LOCKED tag and a yellow square.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lobby-play/v1.mjs log: 'locked leaf rot right after E -0.08 after .05s -0'
findings.fix_correction: The fix is right. Note that game.shrug() may not exist under that name, so reuse whatever F-with-nothing currently calls (the shrug path in Game.action('cable')).

findings.title: Workshop picker leaves the game live: WASD walks Pip away, Tab toggles survey behind it, and the HUD stays up
findings.problem: With the Workshop picker open, holding S walked Pip 4.4 m away and the picker stayed open (lobby-play-45). Tab toggled the survey behind the modal (lobby-play-46). E re-runs interact. The job card, prompt pill and action bar stay visible behind the scrim (lobby-play-18). The picker isn't a pause state: setupInput (src/game.ts:162-166) only gates on paused or atBench, and openPicker (src/hub/lobby.ts:109-116) only swallows Escape. DR-22 says no game key acts while a menu is open. L3 asked that the HUD be hidden behind the picker; that part is still open. A player who reaches for WASD to move through the menu sends Pip wandering, and can end up with the picker open far from the arch.
findings.fix: Add `menu=false` to Game. openPicker sets game.menu=true and body.dataset.menu; close clears both. In setupInput, when this.menu is true, ignore every key except Escape, plus arrow keys and Enter for focus movement within the picker. Clear this.keys. Have step() skip movement while menu. In ui.css: `body[data-menu] .objective, body[data-menu] .prompt-pill, body[data-menu] .hud .actions{visibility:hidden}`. Also auto-close the picker if !nearWorkshop.
findings.verify: Extend tests/lobby.spec.ts 'Workshop arch' with: picker open → advance(1,['KeyS']) and the player doesn't move; press Tab and survey stays false; .objective is hidden.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. With the picker open, holding S for 1 s moved Pip 4.20 m and the picker stayed visible. Tab then set game.survey=true behind the modal. The .objective card and the prompt pill stayed visible. setupInput only gates on atBench and paused (src/game.ts:162-166), and the picker's keydown handler only handles Escape (src/hub/lobby.ts:115).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lobby-play/v2.mjs log: 'picker open S moved 4.20 picker still vis true', 'survey w/ picker true', objective vis true, prompt vis true

findings.title: The Workshop radius steals E from nearby props, and the grab reticle points at a chair while the prompt says Workshop
findings.problem: hub.interact runs before any grab (src/game.ts:198), and nearWorkshop is a 1.6 m circle around (7.5,5.5) (src/hub/lobby.ts:107). The beanbag at (8.6,5.8) (src/levels/lobby.ts:6) is 1.14 m from that point. Standing next to it gives 'E Workshop: practise any station' (script log), and E opens the picker instead of grabbing it. It can only be grabbed from the far side (9.6,6.2). Meanwhile the reticle logic (src/game.ts:432-436) still marks the nearest prop. In lobby-play-17 the yellow grab brackets sit on the red chair while the prompt pill says Workshop. Two cues point at two different things, against DR-42 (the prompt and marker point at the same object) and DR-18.
findings.fix: In Game.render, when this.hub?.prompt() returns a prompt, hide the reticle, or put the reticle on the door or arch threshold instead. Move the beanbag in src/levels/lobby.ts to about (10.8,6.6), or shrink nearWorkshop to 1.2 m, or require Pip to face the arch (dot(heading, toArch) > .5).
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-17: no grab brackets show while the Workshop prompt is up. A script near the beanbag gets 'Grab the bean bag'.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced it. Standing at (7.76,5.21), beside the beanbag, the prompt reads 'E Workshop: practise any station' while the reticle sits on the beanbag at (8.6,5.8). In lobby-play-17 the reticle brackets are on the red chair instead. Either way the two cues point at different things. hub.interact runs before grab (src/game.ts:198), and the reticle is computed separately from the nearest prop (src/game.ts:432-436). The beanbag is 1.14 m from the workshop point, inside the 1.6 m radius (src/hub/lobby.ts:107).
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-lobby-play/v2.mjs log: 'near beanbag W 7.76 5.21 prompt E Workshop… reticle [8.6,5.8]'

findings.title: The hub's three bonus stars are never explained anywhere, and two of them are the same goal
findings.problem: The lobby job card shows three grey stars (lobby-play-01). The code comment in objectives.ts says bonus wording lives 'on the pause and result screens'. The pause card doesn't list bonuses (lobby-play-27), and the hub never reaches a result screen, which is the only place bonuses render (src/ui/game-ui.ts:216-217). So the hub's goals are invisible. Also 'Light every wing' (this.doors.every(d=>d.done)) is identical to 'Finish every job', because door.done is just !!bestFor(id) (src/hub/lobby.ts:45, :47, :73). The third star is free with the first.
findings.fix: Replace 'Light every wing' with a distinct goal: the hub chaos bonus from the empty-hall finding, or 'Earn an A on every bench job'. Render the bonus list on the pause card for every level, including the hub (game-ui.ts paused()), as the result card does. Optionally show them on the directory board as three icon rows.
findings.verify: Open pause in the lobby: three bonus lines are listed with ok or miss. Unit test: with all jobs recorded at grade C, bonus 3 is false while bonus 1 is true.
findings.verify_reason: I read the pause card text in the hub: 'HQ Circuit Crew Hq 0:11 0 0 Resume Restart R Jobs Sound View…'. It has no bonus list. paused() only fills time, damage and cost (src/ui/game-ui.ts:70-72), and bonus lines render only on the result card (:216-217), which the hub never reaches. door.done=!!bestFor(id) (src/hub/lobby.ts:73), so bonus 3 (:47) equals bonus 1 (:45).

findings.title: The pause card in the hub shows a meaningless time/damage/cost tally, title-cases the name to 'Circuit Crew Hq', and has a 'Jobs' button that just reloads the lobby
findings.problem: After knocking a chair and a mug about, the lobby pause card shows 0:14, 2 damage, 30 cost (lobby-play-27). The hub is never graded, so these read as a score the player is losing. Damage is counted in the hub because the generic impact code runs there (src/game.ts:335). The header reads 'Circuit Crew Hq' because title() lowercases every word and re-capitalises the first letter (src/ui/screens.ts:22), and the same would hit any acronym such as QFN. The 'Jobs' button calls toJobs() → ?level=lobby (src/ui/game-ui.ts:76). In the lobby that reloads the same room and resets the toys, which reads as a broken button. This breaks DR-50 (one spelling per name) and DR-22 (buttons do what they say).
findings.fix: screens.ts title(): keep tokens of 3 or fewer letters that are all caps in the source (HQ, QFN) as they are. In the pause markup, when body[data-hub], hide the time, damage and cost stats and the Jobs button (CSS `body[data-hub] .pause .stats, body[data-hub] [data-action=jobs-reload]{display:none}`), or relabel it 'Title'. Optionally turn hub breakage into a playful counter ('Mugs thrown: 2') instead of damage.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-27: the header reads 'Circuit Crew HQ', with no stats row and no Jobs button.
findings.verify_reason: lobby-play-27 shows 'Circuit Crew Hq' with 0:14 / 2 / 30 stats. title() lowercases everything and then capitalises the first letter of each word (src/ui/screens.ts:22). toJobs() goes to ?level=lobby (src/ui/game-ui.ts:76), so in the hub the button just reloads the room. The QFN example is hypothetical: no level name currently contains QFN (that level is 'FABRICATION BAY'), so in practice only HQ is affected. The fix's CSS selector is wrong. The button is `data-ui="jobs-reload"`, not data-action (src/ui/screens.ts:157).
findings.fix_correction: Hide it with `body[data-hub] .pause-screen [data-ui="jobs-reload"]{display:none}`, and hide the stat cells that hold [data-p=time|damage|cost] the same way. body.dataset.hub is already set at src/ui/game-ui.ts:29. title(): keep words that are all caps and 3 letters or fewer as they are (HQ).

findings.title: The lobby never states its one rule: the tagline is unused, the card has no verb, and the spawn prompt is empty
findings.problem: src/levels/lobby.ts:11 defines tagline 'Every door is a job. Pick one.' but nothing renders level taglines. The title shows a fixed line, 'Big offices, springy cables, one small technician.' (src/ui/screens.ts:90). The job goal string 'Circuit Crew HQ: pick a door, fix what's behind it' (src/hub/lobby.ts:42) isn't shown either, because the card shows only dots plus the current step. So a first-time player lands facing the camera, 14 m from a tiny marker, with a card reading '00 · Cable Playground' and nine dots, and no prompt until they happen to walk within 1.5 m of a door (lobby-play-01). Spawn no longer points at a random prop, which is good (L2 fixed for the lobby). But nothing tells the player that doors are the interaction, and the doors look like ordinary office doors.
findings.fix: On first entry (a sessionStorage flag), show the goal line 'Every door is a job: pick one' on the card for 4 s, then collapse to the dots (DR-40 fade). Make the step text a goal, '00 · Cable Playground: walk in', or show the E prompt pill as a ghost ('E at a door to start a job') until the first door is approached. Turn Pip toward the target door at spawn (heading toward doors[0].at).
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-01: at t<4 s the card shows the goal sentence, under 25 words on screen, and Pip faces the marked door.
findings.verify_reason: A grep of src (excluding level files) shows that nothing reads level.tagline. The only 'tagline' outside src/levels/ is the fixed title-screen line (src/ui/screens.ts:90). The job goal string (src/hub/lobby.ts:42) is passed through stationJob but never rendered: the card shows only dots, the step and stars (src/ui/objectives.ts:114-115). lobby-play-01 shows no rule text and no prompt at spawn.

findings.title: The reception board and desk aren't occluders: Pip disappears at a reverse orbit, and the board's bare back shows
findings.problem: The directory board is a 3.3 × 1.6 m black slab at y 1.25–2.85 (src/hub/lobby.ts:59-60), and the desk is a 4 × 1 m block (l.55-57). Neither is registered in game.occluders, and the occlusion ray only tests that list (src/game.ts:387). With the camera orbited behind reception while Pip stands at the desk front, Pip is completely hidden: the 'Grab the mug' prompt is up, but no Pip is on screen (lobby-play-43). The same view shows the board's back as a flat unfinished black plane floating behind the desk with no support (DR-63). The lobby has very few tall objects, so it is a cheap fix, but it is the hub's centrepiece and the orbit is player-controlled.
findings.fix: In Lobby.dress, after building the desk and board, push their meshes into g.occluders with transparent material clones (the decor.ts:55 pattern). Give the board a cream back housing (#efe2c8 box .1 deep with 4 screw dots) and two posts down to the desk top (cyl .04 at x ±1.4, y 1.06→1.25).
findings.verify: Rerun the orbit in f-edges.mjs (orbit 524,-100 at the desk front): Pip is visible through the faded board, and the back of the board shows a housing.
findings.verify_reason: In lobby-play-43, Pip is fully hidden behind the desk and board while the 'Grab the mug' prompt is up. My own orbit (verify-lobby-play-09) shows the board's back as a bare black slab with no housing or posts. G.occluders.length is 0 in the lobby, and src/hub/lobby.ts:55-60 never pushes to occluders.

findings.title: The Workshop arch corner is crowded: the bench runs under the arch pillar, toy cubes sit under the bench, and a coworker stands framed in the arch
findings.problem: The right bench (6.5,3.6), 2 m long (src/hub/lobby.ts:63), ends at x 7.5, inside the arch's footprint. The arch posts are at x 6.5 and 8.5, z 4.3 (l.101-105). The arch's three coloured cubes (l.104, at z 3.8) tuck under the bench seat. The blue coworker at (6.8,1.6) (src/levels/lobby.ts:10) stands right behind the arch, so from the default camera he reads as standing inside the doorway (lobby-play-17). When Pip walks behind the arch, Pip, the bench, the cubes and the blob merge into one blob of shapes (lobby-play-44). audit() returns [] because the solids are 0.2 m apart, but it reads as clutter interpenetrating at the game camera (DR-70 intent).
findings.fix: Move the right bench to (4.6,3.6), or drop it, and mirror the change on the left only if needed. Move the cubes in front of the arch onto its floor mat (z +0.6 local) so they read as 'practice parts'. Move the coworker to (5.6,1.0).
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-17: the arch silhouette is clear, with no bench under its pillar and no blob framed inside it.
findings.verify_reason: Code geometry: the right bench at (6.5,3.6), 2 m long, spans x 5.5–7.5 and z 3.3–3.9 (src/hub/lobby.ts:63). The arch cubes are at z 3.8, x 7.0/7.5/8.0, 0.3 m tall (:104), so the x 7.0 cube sits under the 0.46 m seat. The arch posts are at x 6.5 and 8.5, z 4.3 (:101-105). The blue coworker at (6.8,1.6) (src/levels/lobby.ts:10) is framed inside the arch in lobby-play-17 and verify-lobby-play-07.

findings.title: Footstep dust leaves white pearl-like balls along Pip's path near the back wall
findings.problem: After Pip walks along the back-wall doors, the floor behind him is dotted with white spheres, 10–25 px at the game camera (lobby-play-13, -14, -31: a trail of discs between the Lunch and Rush doors). They fade after a few seconds (none in lobby-play-38 after the settle). They are most likely the footstep dust puffs (src/game.ts:328, a 'dust' burst #e6dfd2 every step). On the warm plank floor they read as dropped pearls or snowballs, not dust: hard-edged, bright and round. This is the kind of particle stacking DR-79 targets.
findings.fix: In the particle 'dust' kind (src/render particles), use a flattened (y .35), soft-edged sprite that grows 0.1→0.35 m while alpha fades 0.45→0 over 0.45 s, tinted toward the floor colour (multiply #d9ab6e). Emit every second step only when not sprinting.
findings.verify: Walk the back wall, then advance(.3) and shot: no bright round discs. Any puffs are soft, low, and gone within 0.5 s.
findings.verify_reason: The white round particles in the shots are real 'dust' puffs: opaque toon icosahedra, size .12–.22, scaling up to 2.8× (src/render/particles.ts:35, :50). Two parts of the claim are wrong. First, they are emitted only while sprinting (pace > 5.5, src/game.ts:327), not every step, and walkTo sprints when d > 2.5 (src/game.ts:473). Second, the long trails in the screenshots are a capture artifact. fx.update runs only in render() (src/game.ts:438), and a ?manual advance() calls render(1/60) once per call, so particles barely age during scripted walks. In real play each puff lives 0.7–1.1 s, so only about 5 show at once. The hard opaque look is still a fair P2 art note.
extra_evidence: src/game.ts:438 + src/game.ts:465 (fx ages only on render; manual advance renders once, so trails freeze in captures)
findings.fix_correction: Don't add 'emit only when not sprinting'. It is already sprint-only, so that change would remove the effect. Instead give 'dust' a transparent MeshBasicMaterial (opacity .45→0, floor-tinted, depthWrite false), the same pattern as 'smoke' (particles.ts:31-33), and flatten it on y. Verify in real time, not with ?manual advance: drop manual, or call render each frame, then sprint and screenshot.

findings.title: The wing lamps, the hub's progress reward, sit above the frame where the default camera crops them, and done doors look like undone ones
findings.problem: Finished doors light a lamp at y 3.35 above the frame header (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97). At the default camera that is the very top edge of the screen. In lobby-play-29 (4 jobs done) the lit lamps are small glows at y about 5–15 px, half cut off. Side-door lamps sit behind the blade-sign bracket. Apart from that, a done door looks the same as an undone one: the same frame, the same closed leaf, and a 0.34 m medal letter that's hard to read. 'Light every wing' should make the room visibly change as the player progresses (the GAME_VISION quote in the file header), but at a glance the lobby with 4 jobs done looks like the lobby with none.
findings.fix: For done doors: put the lamp in front of the header at y 2.9 (z +.3). Give the frame trim an emissive wing-colour glow (hot(color,.6)). Keep the spill wedge on at opacity .2 with the leaf closed. Swap the leaf panel for a 'FIXED ✓' panel in the wing colour, and enlarge the medal per the signage finding. Optionally light a strip of the floor runner from reception to each done door.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-29: a viewer can count the 4 done doors at a glance from the default camera, with HUD hidden.
findings.verify_reason: In lobby-play-29 (4 done) the lit lamps are small glows at the very top edge (about y 5–20 px). The done doors otherwise match the undone ones: same frame and leaf, plus a tiny medal letter. Lamp placement is y 3.35 (src/hub/lobby.ts:96-97).

findings.title: 'WORKSHOP: practise any station' lists only jobs 03–07, and 'station' is never explained
findings.problem: The arch sign and prompt say 'practise any station' (src/hub/lobby.ts:103, :132), and the picker says 'Practise any station…' (l.113). It offers only the five bench jobs 03–07, filtered by l.station && !rush (l.112). A new player doesn't know the word 'station' as a game term (it isn't used on doors, the card or the board), and will wonder why Cable Playground, Big Meeting and Lunch, the jobs they have actually seen, are missing (lobby-play-18). The spelling is now consistent British usage, practise as the verb and Practice as the noun on the result tag, so the L3 spelling item is resolved. The noun is the problem.
findings.fix: Rename it to 'WORKSHOP · bench practice' (sign) and 'Practise a bench job: nothing is graded' (picker). Show 00–02 greyed as 'Cable jobs: walk in, no bench', or support &practice for cable floors too, so 'any' is true.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-18: the wording matches the list, and a first-time reader can say why 00–02 are absent.
findings.verify_reason: lobby-play-18 shows the picker text 'Practise any station…' with only 03–07 listed. The filter is l.station&&!rush (src/hub/lobby.ts:112), and the sign and prompt text are at :103 and :132.

findings.title: Lobby draws 663 calls at start and 693 in survey for a 15-prop room
findings.problem: snap().drawCalls is 663 at the start view and 693 in the survey (script a-views.mjs log), against DR-24's budget of about 250, in the emptiest room in the game. fps holds 60 on the host GPU, but this is the first room on every phone and the budget will be blown as soon as the empty-hall fix adds clutter. Likely sources: 9 doors each with a frame, header, leaf, panel, knob, portal shader plane, spill, threshold, lamp and cap, plus a unique CanvasTexture signPlate for every name, number, medal and board row (about 40 plates), each drawn twice through the outline pass.
findings.fix: Merge the static door parts per material per wall (BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries after dress(); the leaf stays separate), put all sign text into one atlas CanvasTexture with UV offsets, instance the 9 lamps, cap sockets and knobs, and draw the board rows into one canvas. Target ≤ 250 at the start view.
findings.verify: Rerun a-views.mjs: drawCalls ≤ 250 at start and survey, with the visuals unchanged.
findings.verify_reason: I measured renderer.info.render.calls at 600 for the start view and 680 for the survey, close to the reviewer's 663/693 and well over DR-24's ~250 for a 15-prop room. The suspected sources (per-door parts plus a unique signPlate per label) match src/hub/lobby.ts:84-98 and :59-60, but I did not break down the attribution.

findings.title: Title screen still shows the unclear 'HQ' badge on Play and a faint gamepad indicator (L4 still open)
findings.problem: R3A N12 (L4) is unchanged. The Play button carries a grid icon plus 'HQ' sub-badge with no meaning to a new player, next to a second grid button that opens the Jobs board, so two near-identical grid icons sit side by side (lobby-play-00). The gamepad indicator at bottom right (screens.ts:102 `.padind`) renders at about 20% opacity and looks disabled or broken, also on a phone (lobby-play-33). The title's hero framing of Pip beside the logo (P7) is good and has not regressed.
findings.fix: Label Play as just 'Play' (drop the HQ badge), give the Jobs button a different icon (a list or board) with a text label 'Jobs', and hide `.padind` until a 'gamepadconnected' event fires.
findings.verify: Retake lobby-play-00 and -33: one grid-like icon at most, no faint gamepad glyph without a pad.
findings.verify_reason: lobby-play-00 shows Play with a grid disc and an 'HQ' badge, next to an identical grid Jobs button. The badge is the lobby's disc(l) plus number 'HQ' (src/ui/screens.ts:84-88). The pad indicator is dim without a pad, but its opacity is .45, not about 20% (src/ui/screens.css:46). It only turns on through syncPad (src/ui/game-ui.ts:144).
findings.fix_correction: Hide it with `.padind:not(.on){display:none}` in src/ui/screens.css (syncPad already toggles .on), rather than adding a new gamepadconnected listener.

notes.fun: What works: the lobby is quick and snappy. Spawn to the farthest door is about 3.2 s, any door to any other 3.0–4.0 s, and a door to the loaded job about 1.4 s, so there is no dead walking (DR-09 passes). Chaos is responsive: grabbing the red chair and throwing it (Q) at reception sent it over the desk at 8.4 m/s, popped the receptionist's '!' alarm bubble within 0.5 s (DR-04 passes) and counted damage, and a thrown mug also alarmed. Doors swing open on a springy overshoot as Pip nears, light spills onto the floor, and the interior-mapped portal shows real parallax and a thumbnail of the destination room (lobby-play-11, -30). That is charming and the best thing in the room. What doesn't: the hub is mostly empty floor with 15 props and no cable, so the game's star mechanic is missing from the room players see most. There's no chaos goal and nothing happens on its own in the first 30 s. Entering a door is an instant reload with no walk-in or fade, and coming back resets Pip to spawn with no wing-lamp ignition, so the progression payoff ('a wing lights up') never plays on screen. Done doors are hard to tell from undone ones at the default camera.
notes.playability: Navigation works and nothing soft-locks: all 9 doors are reachable, the locked Arcade Rush door gives a clear prompt and unlocks once the Arcade has a result (verified by seeding localStorage, lobby-play-31), the front edge has an invisible wall at z 9.5, a crate carried to a door just drops on E and a second E enters, the Workshop picker launches practice, and Esc closes it without opening pause. audit(.02) returns [] and every script closed with zero console or page errors (DR-80 passes). The big playability problem is the door leaves. They swing toward the camera and cover Pip completely at all three side doors (and on phone), and half-cover him at back-wall doors, right at the moment of choosing. The reception board and desk also hide Pip from a reverse orbit because the lobby registers no occluders. On a phone, both the start view and the Tab survey show only 3 of 9 doors and the target is off-screen. The Workshop picker doesn't block game input: WASD walks Pip away and Tab toggles survey behind it. The Workshop's 1.6 m radius steals E from the beanbag beside it. Performance is 60 fps but 663–693 draw calls for 15 props.
notes.clarity: The prompt pill is good: it names the door and number, the best grade, and what a locked door needs ('Locked: finish 03 · Overheating Arcade first'). There's no stray 'Grab the cone' prompt at spawn any more. Signage, which the hub depends on, doesn't read at the game camera: door names are 5–8 px cap height, numbers, LOCKED and medals 4–6 px, and side-door blade signs about 4 px and partly hidden under the job card. Each side door has two crossed signs. The objective marker is a pale 20 px unoutlined cone inside the door frame and gets lost easily, with no off-screen arrow. The lobby's one rule ('Every door is a job. Pick one.') is defined as the level tagline but never shown; the card reads only '00 · Cable Playground' with nine dots and three unexplained grey stars, whose wording never appears anywhere in the hub, and one bonus duplicates another. The pause card shows a meaningless damage and cost tally, 'Circuit Crew Hq', and a Jobs button that reloads the lobby. 'Practise any station' uses jargon and lists only 5 of 9 jobs. The title still has the unclear HQ badge and the faint gamepad glyph.
notes.teaching: The hub teaches no electronics, by design. A missed opportunity: a small 8 m hub reel that lights the HQ sign would let the first act in the game be the cable act (length, plug-snap) before the Playground, and would satisfy AGENTS 4 in the hub.
notes.models: Not this reviewer's dimension. In passing: the directory board's back is a bare black slab floating behind the desk with no support (lobby-play-43). The blade-sign bracket stops short of the wall. The portal corridor shader reads well. Pip, chairs, plants and coworkers read cleanly at the game camera. Floor luma is 165–177, inside DR-54's 140–185.
